subparts.method: Derive the squared norm of the coefficient pair independently. With positive source amplitudes,the resultant amplitude is its nonnegative square root,and lies between|a−b|and a+b.

subparts.author_conclusion: The resultant need not have a greater amplitude. At a=b=1,c=π,it is identicallyzero; at a=2,b=1,c=π,it has amplitude1,smaller than the first constituent.
subparts.author_derivation: R²=a²+b²+2abcosc. For positive a,b,cosc∈[−1,1]gives|a−b|≤R≤a+b. In particular cancellation is allowed by the unrestricted question. The printed sentence claiming a greater amplitude is therefore false without additional restrictions.
subparts.method: Author mathematical reasoning from the original task; explicit source support/absence recorded. This logical comparison is not an automated proof.

subparts.author_conclusion: For R>0,a correct phase satisfiescosε=P/R,sinε=Q/R,so choose a quadrant-aware atan2(Q,P),modulo2π. The printedatan(Q/P)alone loses quadrants and is undefined on the vertical axis.
subparts.author_derivation: Takea=1,b=3,c=π:thenP=−2,Q=0andI=−2sinx. A positive-amplitude sine needsεπmodulo2π,butatan(Q/P)=0. Takea=1,b=2,c=2π/3:thenP=0,Q=√3andI=√3cosx,soεπ/2;Q/Pis undefined. IfR=0,no resultant phase is defined. These cases are all permitted by the source question.
subparts.method: Author mathematical reasoning from the original task; explicit source support/absence recorded. This logical comparison is not an automated proof.

subparts.author_conclusion: For nonzero resultant and f>0,the fundamental frequency remainsf. A phase-between claim requires compatible representatives and a stated phase-difference convention; zero resultant has no fundamental oscillation frequency or phase.
subparts.author_derivation: Both terms reduce toPsin(2πft)+Qcos(2πft). If(P,Q)≠(0,0),this is a nonzero sinusoid with the same angular rate. If(P,Q)=(0,0),the function is zero and every shift is a period,so it has no positive fundamental period. For positive amplitudes and a phase difference in(−π,π),the positive vector sum lies between the two rays on that chosen shorter arc. The printed question sets no such representative convention; phase comparison as an ordered interval is incomplete at the opposite-ray/zero cases and modulo2π.
